questions.q: What is a computed column, such as TotalPrice AS (Quantity * UnitPrice)?
options: A column you must manually update with a trigger
A column that stores a running total across all rows
A column that can only hold NULL values
A column whose value is calculated from other columns in the same row
questions.explain: The expression in parentheses is evaluated using other columns in that same row — here, Quantity times UnitPrice.

questions.q: Is a plain computed column (without PERSISTED) stored on disk?
options: It's stored, but only in a separate hidden table
Only the first value is stored, then it stops updating
No — it's virtual, recalculated on the fly every time it's read
Yes, exactly like any other ordinary column
questions.explain: By default a computed column is virtual: SQL Server works out its value whenever a query reads it, rather than storing it.

questions.q: What does adding PERSISTED to a computed column change?
options: It prevents the column from ever being updated again
It removes the expression and stores a fixed constant instead
SQL Server physically stores the value on disk and keeps it in sync automatically
It converts the column into a regular, directly-insertable column
questions.explain: PERSISTED tells SQL Server to compute and store the value physically, updating it whenever the underlying columns change.

questions.q: Why would you want a computed column to be PERSISTED?
options: Only PERSISTED columns can use arithmetic expressions
PERSISTED columns use less storage than virtual ones
PERSISTED is required before you can INSERT into the table at all
A PERSISTED computed column can be indexed, unlike a purely virtual one
questions.explain: Indexing requires an actual stored value to point at, which only a PERSISTED computed column has.

questions.q: Can you directly INSERT a value into a computed column?
options: No — its value is always derived from the expression, not supplied directly
Yes, and doing so overrides the expression permanently
Yes, but only on the first row of the table
Yes, as long as the column is PERSISTED
questions.explain: A computed column's value always comes from evaluating its expression — you can't write directly into it.
